content.title: About
content.content: Eggs are the reproductive cells of birds, most commonly consumed chicken eggs. They have a hard shell and contain the white (albumen) and yolk, which is rich in fats, vitamins, and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are a complete source of protein, containing all essential amino acids.
A typical large chicken egg weighs about 50 g and provides roughly 70 kcal.
The yolk contains almost all B‑vitamins, vitamin D, and choline, which is important for brain health.
Eggs can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 4–5 weeks when kept properly.
In cooking, eggs serve as a binding, leavening, and emulsifying agent.

items.title: Rich source of high‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs provide fully digestible protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains essential vitamins and minerals
items.content: The yolk supplies vitamins A, D, E, K and minerals such as iron, phosphorus, and selenium.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in the yolk help protect eyes from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: High protein content helps you feel full longer, which may aid weight management.

items.title: Supports brain function
items.content: Choline found in the yolk is vital for memory and cognitive function.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may develop an allergy to eggs, ranging from skin reactions to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Risk of Salmonella
items.content: Raw or undercooked eggs can harbor Salmonella bacteria, so they should be cooked thoroughly.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: The yolk contains cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume eggs in moderation.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Do not leave eggs at room temperature for more than 2 hours; use only intact, uncracked eggs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eggs can be boiled, fried, poached, scrambled, or used in baking, omelets, casseroles, and sauces. They are also added to salads, soups, and desserts. For a softer texture, try poached eggs or soft‑scrambled eggs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store eggs in the refrigerator in their original carton, preferably in the egg compartment, at 1–4 °C. Fresh eggs keep for 3–4 weeks. Do not wash eggs before storing, as this removes their natural protective coating.
